messages:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: latency SLO breach in us-west-2-serving (p95/p99 elevated, streaming stalls). AlertID=INC-513999. Paging on-call now.

Priya Sharma: acknowledged, I'm on it. Adding triage channels: #eng-oncall and #eng-runtime. Who's seeing metrics?

Matt O'Connor: grabbing dashboards. p95 from baseline ~120ms -> 480ms over last 15m. p99 jumping from ~1.2s -> 3.6s. Streaming stalls count up 8x.

Cheng Wu: logs show a burst of KV evictions and slab compaction spikes around 15:05. Many prefill tasks queued while decode workers starved. Looks like fragmentation followed by aggressive eviction.

Lina Torres: can we throttle prefill or reduce concurrency quickly? I can push a hot config if we agree.

Jamal Patel: customer impact note: Support reports timeouts for streaming RPCs for Customer-A and Customer-B in us-west-2. Tickets raised. No widespread 5xxs but degraded quality.

Priya Sharma: action plan: 1) reduce PREFILL_MAX_CONCURRENCY from 12 -> 4, 2) enable soft compaction to reduce slab fragmentation, 3) route ~20% traffic to fallback model-variant (lower mem footprint) to relieve pressure. 

Matt O'Connor: running command to patch config for prefill on pool serving-usw2-1:

```
redwoodctl pools update serving-usw2-1 --set PREFILL_MAX_CONCURRENCY=4
```

Matt O'Connor: applied. PREFILL queue length dropping.

Cheng Wu: also submitted a hotfix to eviction thresholds to be less aggressive while compaction runs. Patch: bump kv_eviction_low_watermark from 0.65 -> 0.72.

Lina Torres: applying compaction toggle now: `kvctl compact --pool serving-usw2-1 --mode soft`

ops-bot: compaction job started (job id comp-513999-1). Estimated time ~3m.

Matt O'Connor: metrics update 2m after changes: p95 -> 210ms, p99 -> 1.1s, streaming stalls down 60%. Good but not back to baseline.

Jamal Patel: notifying affected customers: posted interim status to Customer-A and Customer-B. Mentioned fallback routing and that we're monitoring. No ETA yet.

Priya Sharma: routing 20% to model-variant-mem-slim: `routes update serving-route-123 --fallback model-variant-mem-slim --weight 20`

Matt O'Connor: routing applied. Traffic shifted. Latency trending down further. p95 ~160ms, p99 ~720ms.

Cheng Wu: root cause hypothesis so far: KV cache slab fragmentation + a sudden prefill surge from a batch of long-sequence requests (external job) created large variable-length entries. This caused frequent evictions and decode workers experienced imbalanced load (prefill tasks queued, decode CPU underutilized), producing tail stalls.

Lina Torres: note — prefill vs decode imbalance should be instrumented. We'll add queue depth and worker utilization alarms.

Matt O'Connor: quick logs showing eviction rate before/after:

```
[15:04:02] eviction_rate=520/s slab_free_frag=0.12 active_prefill_tasks=240 decode_workers_idle=18
[15:09:40] eviction_rate=48/s slab_free_frag=0.35 active_prefill_tasks=32 decode_workers_idle=2
```

Priya Sharma: ops-bot please create incident record and handoff to next on-call in 30m. Lina, you'll take the next shift. Lina, capture any followups and runbook updates.

ops-bot: Incident INC-513999 created. Severity=P1. Handoff scheduled to Lina Torres at 5139991800.

Lina Torres: taking ownership at handoff time. Summary for handoff: mitigation applied (prefill throttled, eviction tuned, soft compaction, 20% fallback routing). Customer impact limited to degraded streaming quality for Customer-A/B and transient increased p99. Current state: p95 ~150-180ms, p99 ~600-800ms, streaming stalls reduced ~75%.

Jamal Patel: I'll follow up with CS to confirm customers seeing improvements and close tickets if stable.

Cheng Wu: next steps for postmortem: 1) reproduce prefill surge with variable-length sequences in staging to trigger fragmentation, 2) add proactive compaction and a reactive auto-throttle for prefill when eviction rate crosses threshold, 3) add alert for prefill:decode imbalance (queue depth vs worker utilization), 4) consider adaptive slab resizing.

Priya Sharma: agreed. Also assign owners: Matt -> short-term metrics/rollback playbook, Cheng -> implement auto-throttle and alarm, Lina -> runbook updates + postmortem writeup, Jamal -> customer comms closure.

incident-bot: Update logged: mitigation actions applied. Monitoring window 30m.

Lina Torres: leaving notes for on-call rotation: if latency resurges, revert prefill concurrency to 2 and route additional traffic out of us-west-2 until compaction completes.

Matt O'Connor: snapshotting dashboards and saving logs to /incidents/INC-513999/artifacts.

Priya Sharma: great work team. We'll keep this pinned for the postmortem.

(End of thread)
